metadata.description: Moves the DSH sidebar account avatar out of the bottom strip: four placements (including a zero-height inline mode), three heights, and a settings card on the Plugins page.
metadata.name: dsh-avatar-top

paragraphs.text: Moves the DSH sidebar account avatar out of the bottom strip: four placements (including a zero-heig
ht inline mode), three heights, and a settings card on the Plugins page.
# dsh-avatar-top
English | 中文

Moves the left sidebar's account avatar (which is also the Settings launcher) out of the bottom
stri

p, so the session list gains the space back. Placement, height and spacing are adjustable from
a car
d on the **Plugins** page; **inline brand row** costs zero vertical space.

> Tested against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` (desktop, Windows). The macOS desktop is left
> untou
ched by design; the browser shell works on every platform.
Two fixes that only show up on a real desktop:

- The Windows titlebar strip is a `-webkit-app-region: drag` band (DSH paints it with
`[data-windows

-titlebar] .frame:before`). The inline avatar used to sit inside it, so a click
started a window dra

g. The container and the button now opt out with `no-drag`.
- The desktop shell snapshots the inject

ion table at Host start, so the boot `<style>` row could
not be removed when the plugin was switched

off — the switch looked dead. Every selector is now
gated on `:not([data-avatar-top-off])`, an attr
ibute the browser half toggles on `<html>`.
## What it does

DSH pins a footer at the bottom of the left sidebar: the account row (`头像 + 账号名`) sits next to
`side
bar.footer.action`, where plugins such as `dsh-cost-meter` mount their own widgets.
This plugin moves **only the account row**:

- The footer becomes `display: contents`, so its two children join the sidebar's flex column; the
ac

count row is then reordered while `_footerActions` keeps its default order and stays pinned at
the b

ottom. (Moving the whole footer would drag other plugins' widgets along — that was a real
bug in 0.2

.1.)
- Four placements: **top**, **below the brand row**, **below New Session**, or **inline inside

the
brand row** (Windows desktop; `position: absolute` at the free right end, zero vertical cost).
-

Three heights: **full 44px**, **compact 32px**, **avatar only 28px** (hides the account name and
sh

rinks the avatar to 20px).
- Spacing 0–24px, and an on/off switch that restores the stock layout wit

hout uninstalling.
- The desktop update pill (download progress / "ready") shares that flex row. Whi

le it is visible the
**inline** placement temporarily returns to a normal 28px row under the brand r

ow: an absolutely
positioned row has no width to give the pill, so it would otherwise be drawn under

neath the
avatar. The avatar goes back to the corner as soon as the pill disappears.

Changes apply immediately — the browser half subscribes to the settings document and rewrites the
st

ylesheet. Switching the plugin off is immediate too: the boot row a desktop session baked in at
Host

start is gated on `data-avatar-top-off`, so it goes inert without a restart. Settings persist
in th
e profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.
## Settings
| Setting | Values | Default |

| Enabled | on / off | on |
| Position | top / below brand / below New Session / inline brand row |

top |
| Height | full 44 / compact 32 / avatar only 28 | full 44 |
| Spacing below | 0–24 px | 4 |
|
Restore defaults | button | — |
## Install
Not on npm yet — install from GitHub:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart DSH once after installing (the client bundle and package metadata are read at host start).
T
hen open **Plugins → dsh-avatar-top** to configure it.
The npm name `dsh-avatar-top` is reserved; once published, `dsh plugin add dsh-avatar-top` works too
he npm name `dsh-avatar-top` is reserved; once published, `dsh plugin add dsh-avatar-top` works too.

Self-check: the plugin serves its current stylesheet at `/dsh-avatar-top.css` (public, read-only),
s
o a wrong layout can be diagnosed without a session:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## How it works
### Injection channel
The Host contributes one structured `style` row through `webserver/index-inject`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Both shells render that row:
| Shell | Where the page comes from | How the row arrives |
| Browser / `dsh web` | the SPA dist server answers the index over HTTP | `renderIndex()` renders th

e rows into the HTML |
| Desktop app | Electron serves `dsh-web-frontend/dist/index.html` itself ove
r its `dsh-app://` scheme | the Host's injection table is handed to the page over IPC after startup;
the page-side interpreter appends `style` rows to `<head>` |
`ctx.webServer.tapIndex()` would only cover the HTTP shell; the desktop window never calls it.

The desktop snapshot is taken at Host start, so the browser half also applies the stylesheet live
(`

<style id="dsh-avatar-top-live">`, appended after the boot row, so it wins) and the boot row only
pr
events a flash on first paint.
### The rule

The sidebar is a flex column; placement is pure `order`, and selectors key off the stable
CSS-module

class-name suffixes (`_root`, `_footArea`, `_settingsArea`, `_trigger`, `_label`,
`_avatar`, `_logo

Row`, `_newSession`, `_panelList`) rather than the per-build hash prefix.
`_trigger` / `_label` / `_

avatar` come from the settings-account module (`AccountMenu`); the rest
from ui-sidebar.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- macOS keeps its traffic-light strip layout (`:not([data-platform='darwin'])`).
- Collapsed rails a

re left untouched (on Windows the footer is `display:none` there anyway).
- `inlineBrand` lifts the

button out of the flow (`top: 8px; right: 12px; z-index: 3`) and forces
the avatar-only shape. On no

n-Windows shells it falls back to `top`. The band it lands in is the
`titleBarOverlay` drag strip, s

o both the row and the button carry `-webkit-app-region: no-drag`.
While the update pill exists (`:h

as([class*='_indicator'])`) the row returns to
`position: static; order: -3`, i.e. a normal 28px row

under the brand row.
- The button selector is
`[class*='_trigger']:not([class*='_triggerRow']):not(

[class*='_triggerLabel'])`. A bare
`[class*='_trigger']` also matches `_triggerRow` — the flex row h

olding the account button, the
connection indicator and the update pill — which collapsed the row to

28px and drew the pill
underneath the avatar (0.3.0 bug). The row itself only gets `flex-wrap: wrap

`, so a pill that
